summary: Creates IANA registries for code points used in MPLS LSP Ping, including Downstream Mapping flags, multipath types, pad TLVs and address types. These had been defined in RFCs 4379 and 6424 without registries. It was replaced by RFC 8029.

eli5.summary: A notebook where every special code used by a network testing tool gets written down, so nobody picks the same code for different meanings. It was later replaced by RFC 8029.

subtitle: Creates IANA registries for four sets of MPLS LSP Ping code points that earlier RFCs left unregistered.

tldr.problem: RFC 4379 and RFC 6424 created name spaces for MPLS LSP Ping but never created IANA registries for DS Flags, Multipath Types, Pad TLVs, and Interface and Label Stack Address Types, and new allocations were now needed.
tldr.mechanism: The document asks IANA to create those four registries, with registration policies and initial assignments taken from the earlier RFCs.
tldr.outcome: New code points could be assigned in an orderly way. It has since been obsoleted by RFC 8029.

today: RFC 7537 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 8029, which now holds the definition of these registries.

sections.title: Why the Registries Were Needed
sections.content:
RFC 4379 and RFC 6424 defined name spaces for MPLS LSP Ping, but did not create the matching IANA registries for DS Flags, Multipath Types, Pad TLVs, and Interface and Label Stack Address Types. Two other documents then in progress asked for new DS Flags and Multipath Type allocations, so there was a need to make further allocations.

RFC 7537 updates RFC 4379 and RFC 6424 by creating these registries. It notes that DS Flags and Multipath Type are fields in two TLVs: Downstream Mapping (value 2, deprecated) and Downstream Detailed Mapping (value 20). A change to either registry therefore affects both TLVs.
sections.eli5: People wanted to add new codes, but there was no official list to add them to. This document starts the lists.

sections.title: Registry Rules and Starting Values
sections.content:
All four registries are created inside the existing "Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS) Label Switched Paths (LSPs) Ping Parameters" registry group.

The DS Flags registry uses Standards Action. Bit 7 is N (treat as a non-IP packet) and bit 6 is I (interface and label stack object request), both from RFC 4379. Bits 5 to 0 are unassigned.

The other three registries share one policy: values 0 to 250 by Standards Action, 251 to 254 for Experimental Use, and 255 by Standards Action.

  • Multipath Types: 0 no multipath, 2 IP address, 4 IP address range, 8 bit-masked IP address set, 9 bit-masked label set. Values 251 to 254 are Experimental Use and 255 is Reserved.
  • Pad Types: 0 Reserved, 1 drop the Pad TLV from the reply, 2 copy the Pad TLV to the reply, 251 to 254 Experimental Use, 255 Reserved.
  • Interface and Label Stack Address Types: 0 Reserved, 1 IPv4 Numbered, 2 IPv4 Unnumbered, 3 IPv6 Numbered, 4 IPv6 Unnumbered, 251 to 254 Experimental Use, 255 Reserved.
sections.eli5: Each notebook has some pages already filled in from the old documents. Some page numbers are kept for experiments, and new official codes need a proper standards document.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document says it simply creates IANA registries for code points already defined in RFC 4379 and RFC 6424, so it raises no new security concerns.
sections.eli5: Making a list of codes that already existed does not open any new doors for trouble.

sections.title: Relationship to Other RFCs
sections.content: RFC 7537 is a Standards Track document that updates RFC 4379 and RFC 6424. Its own metadata shows it was later obsoleted by RFC 8029, so the current definition of these registries should be read there.
sections.eli5: This list was later replaced by a newer document, so the newer one is the one to check.
